description: Shared foundation for every account type. Not selectable on its own.
_note: ONLY things true of every single employee belong here.
Anything that differs between salaried and hourly belongs in base-salaried or
base-hourly instead. Licence groups in particular are NOT universal - because
groups are additive, putting E3 here would give hourly staff both E3 and F3.

_attributeNotes: company      -> holds the shift, per site convention
employeeNumber is a first-class AD attribute (dedicated New-ADUser parameter)
extensionAttribute1 is what Exchange Online calls CustomAttribute1
ad._namingNote: Username generation is NOT configured here. It lives in the 'naming' block of config.json so that one set of rules governs AD, the WMS and anything added later. A role may override it with its own top-level 'naming' block.
ad._upnNote: UPN suffix is NOT set here. It comes from defaultUpnSuffix in config.json so there is one place to change it. Add "upnSuffix" to a specific role only if that role genuinely needs a different one - it will override the default.

_promptNotes: Inherited by every role, so these two fields appear on every account type.

prompts.name: EmployeeNumber
prompts.label: Employee number
prompts._validationNote: Variable-length digits. Tighten the range if you know the real bounds, e.g. ^[0-9]{5,7}$
prompts.validationMessage: Employee number must contain digits only, with no spaces or letters.

_promptExample._howToUse: Copy this object into the 'prompts' array below to activate it. Options may be plain strings (label and value identical) or {label, value} objects. The operator picks the label; AD, SQL and tokens all receive the value. The label is also available as {EmployeeClass_label}.
_promptExample.name: EmployeeClass
_promptExample.label: Employee class
